reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown explain Joshua's absence from the Numbers 14:24 oath as an omission, not exclusion, since he stood outside the ranks as Moses' constant attendant.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Wells reads the oath's wording at face value, since Numbers 14:24 names Caleb alone as the exception while the surrounding verses count both Caleb and Joshua among the survivors.

sides.snippet: but my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and has followed me fully, him will I bring into the land
sides.verseText: but my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and has followed me fully, him will I bring into the land into which he went; and his seed shall possess it.

sides.snippet: Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, remained alive of those men who went to spy out the land
sides.verseText: But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, remained alive of those men who went to spy out the land.
